steps.title: Database schema and data module
steps.headline: Schema and data module are sound; dependency approved; document the additions and configure the build gates.
judge_reasons: The goal is met. src/schema.sql defines users, sessions and tasks with the required columns. It uses an autoincrement id, a UNIQUE e-mail with CHECK (email = lower(email)), and REFERENCES foreign keys on sessions.user_id, tasks.owner_id and tasks.created_by. src/db.js turns on `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` in openDb, and a test asserts the pragma value is 1.
The schema applies twice because every statement uses IF NOT EXISTS, and the test in tests/db.test.js covers it.
The tests cover the required cases: a duplicate e-mail is rejected by UNIQUE, a null title or owner by NOT NULL, and a non-existent owner by FOREIGN KEY.

The due date is optional (`due_date TEXT` with no NOT NULL), and the tests check it is optional but kept when given. This follows the product-owner decision to allow NULL. Replacing the due-date NOT NULL test with an optional-date test is therefore required by the step, not a loosened test.

Security rules are followed. Every statement in src/db.js is parameterised with `?`, and the only SQL read from a file is the fixed schema. No function deletes a member. The only delete-like export is deleteSession, and a test pins the delete/remove/drop export list to exactly that. The foreign keys have no ON DELETE action, so deleting a referenced user is refused by default.
The acceptance test file tests/acceptance/criteria.test.js is not in the diff, so it is unchanged. The coder reports it is still skipped.

The `users.display_name` column is not in the step's column list, but the display-name decision presupposes it, and the coder flagged it. The length CHECKs on display_name and title are small unrequested additions and are not worth rejecting. The dependency is pinned, and package.json and the lockfile are the expected install side effects.

steps.title: Registration, login, logout and the 10-member cap
steps.headline: Auth step works and tests pass, but test fixtures need clarity and server.js needs coverage
judge_reasons: All six product-owner decisions are followed. Register logs the member in and redirects 303 to / (src/server.js POST /register). Logout redirects to /login?loggedout=1, which shows 'You are logged out.'. A logged-in person opening /login or /register is redirected to /. E-mail is trimmed and lower-cased, at most 254 characters, with one @ and text on both sides (auth.js isValidEmail). Duplicate e-mail gets 409 and a failed login gets 401, each with the exact message and the typed e-mail kept. A full team shows the message with 200 on GET and 409 on POST. A foreign Origin gets 403 'Cross-site request refused.' and a missing Origin is allowed (auth.js originCheck).

Security notes are met. Passwords use scrypt with a 16-byte random salt and timingSafeEqual. registerMember runs the count check, the duplicate check, the user insert and the first session in one db.transaction(...).immediate(). Only the SHA-256 of the session token is stored. The cookie is httpOnly and SameSite=Lax. An unknown e-mail verifies against a dummy hash and returns the same 401 message as a wrong password. Output goes through esc(). SQL goes through the db.js helpers, with no raw SQL built from strings.

Tests cover every item in the step's test list: register then login, wrong password, logout invalidating the session, the 11th registration creating no user, concurrent last-place registrations, duplicate e-mail and foreign Origin. C1 is un-skipped with its name unchanged and only its body filled in. The other acceptance tests are still skipped, and no assertion was loosened.

The extras are small and support the step: a minimal / page so redirects have a target, and listening when the file is run directly. The coder flagged both, along with the placeholder wording for validation errors and the non-sliding sessions, which deviates from DECISIONS.md but needs no schema change.

Minor note: auth.js userForToken parses created_at with new Date(). If the column holds a SQLite 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' string with no timezone, JS reads it as local time and expiry can be off by the UTC offset. This is not blocking.

steps.title: Reassign a task
steps.headline: Reassign works and is secure, but views.js has no unit tests and credentials in test files need clarification.
judge_reasons: `src/tasks.js` adds `POST /tasks/:id/owner` behind `requireLogin`. It validates the new owner on the server with `ID_PATTERN` and `findUserById` before writing. A non-member gets 400 with 'Owner must be a member.' shown above the list, and the task is unchanged, which matches the product owner's decisions.

`reassignTask` runs a single parameterized `UPDATE tasks SET owner_id = ? WHERE id = ?` inside a transaction, so only `owner_id` changes. `tests/tasks-reassign.test.js` checks this with `toEqual({ ...before, owner_id: 2 })`.

Any logged-in member can reassign, with no creator or owner check, as the step requires. The test 'a member who is neither creator nor owner can reassign' covers it. Choosing the same owner redirects to `/` and leaves the task untouched, and the 'same owner is harmless' test covers that.

`src/views.js` adds a picker with the current owner preselected and a 'Reassign' button on each task row. Done tasks are not listed yet, which the coder disclosed. That is a later step, so this is not scope creep.
C3 in `criteria.test.js` was un-skipped and implemented with real assertions: the owner is 1 after a GET, then 2 after the reassign. No test was removed, loosened or skipped.

Tests cover 401 without a session, 403 on a foreign Origin, 404 for a bad task id, and junk or missing owner values, which meets the step's security notes. The diff contains no secrets and no raw SQL built from strings.
The coder did not update the docs files and said so openly. This is not part of the step's goal or test.

The step goal is met. src/views.js adds an always-present `

Done

The one edit to an existing test, in tests/tasks-done.test.js, checks only the part of the page above the Done heading. That is needed because done tasks now appear on the same page, so it adapts the test rather than weakening it. No test was removed or skipped.

steps.title: Security hardening and offline guarantees
steps.headline: Security headers and error handling are in place and tested. Verify test fixtures are not real secrets; add direct unit tests for server.js and views.js.
judge_reasons: Goal and test are met. `securityHeaders` in src/server.js sets a same-origin CSP (`default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`), X-Content-Type-Options and X-Frame-Options DENY on every response. It is registered before `originCheck`, so refused cross-site posts carry the headers too.

The error pages match the decisions. An unknown address returns 404 'Page not found.' with a link to the list. An unexpected failure returns 500 'Something went wrong. Nothing was saved.' with a link. The detail goes only to `console.error`, not to the client (`errorHandler`, `failurePage`).
Unauthenticated POSTs to task routes return 401 'Please log in.' and GETs redirect with 302. tests/security.test.js asserts both, plus that a refused submit changes nothing.

The login throttle follows the decision. `createLoginLimiter` is in memory and per e-mail. The 5th failure blocks that e-mail for 15 minutes, and `loginHandler` returns 429 'Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.' The tests cover the block, the lift after 15 minutes, other e-mails being unaffected, the window expiring and a success clearing the count.
No existing test was removed or loosened. Only the new tests/security.test.js was added, and the protected acceptance file is untouched.
Scope is contained. The `now` clock parameter on `createApp` and the two view helpers exist to support the throttle and the error pages. The docs updates are routine.

Security: no secrets or credentials appear in the diff, and passwords and e-mails are not logged. Omitting HSTS and the Secure cookie flag is explained and flagged as depending on the undecided HTTPS choice, in line with the step's security notes.

It explains restoring with the server stopped first, copying the file over data/tasks.db, then starting again. It warns that the database file holds password hashes.
